approved: With fixed margins, Fisher's exact test evaluates the hypergeometric count law under the null.
The Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel statistic uses an asymptotic chi-square reference under appropriate stratified conditions.
Pearson's test of independence compares its statistic to a chi-square reference under large-sample regularity.
The F-test evaluates an F statistic against the reference F distribution in the applicable model.
Under paired t-test assumptions, the standardized mean of the paired differences follows Student t under the null.
Under the common covariance and normality conditions, the two-sample T-squared statistic has the Hotelling reference law.
The Breslow–Day statistic is evaluated with its asymptotic chi-square reference.
The one-sample Hotelling test uses the T-squared reference distribution under multivariate normality.
Tukey's HSD calibrates comparisons using the studentized range.
The Newman–Keuls range procedure uses the studentized range reference law.
The exact hypergeometric test uses the hypergeometric reference law for counts under its conditioning model.
The exact binomial test evaluates the count under the specified binomial null.
The one-sample t-test evaluates its statistic under the reference t law with the stated sampling assumptions.
The pooled test uses a t reference under equal population variances and normal-sample conditions.
Welch's unequal-variance test uses an approximate t reference with Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.
The Pearson goodness-of-fit statistic uses an asymptotic chi-square reference under its count and model conditions.
Cochran's Q for matched binary proportions has an asymptotic chi-square reference under its null.
The Hosmer–Lemeshow statistic is conventionally assessed using an approximate chi-square reference.
The Sidik–Jonkman procedure estimates between-study heterogeneity variance in random-effects meta-analysis.
The Hunter–Schmidt record is linked to the between-study variance estimand in its stated meta-analysis context.
The DerSimonian–Laird method estimates between-study variance.
Model parameter estimation yields an estimate of its model parameter in the documented setting.
The STATO likelihood estimation restriction identifies a model parameter estimate as the method output.
The source refers to the best linear unbiased estimator for a parameter in its applicable linear model.
The method explicitly outputs a confidence interval, an interval estimate with a defined model and coverage convention.
The PLS regression fit yields coefficients for its prediction equation within its model context.
The standardized Z statistic is used to evaluate the Z-test. The source models the statistic as an input distinct from the normal reference distribution.
The F statistic is the test statistic of the scoped F-test. The input role names the statistic and the separately reviewed reference-law projection retains the F distribution.
The paired t procedure uses the t statistic computed on paired differences under its ordinary application conditions.
The one-sample t procedure uses the t statistic formed from a sample mean and estimated standard error.
The pooled two-sample t procedure uses a t statistic with a pooled estimate of variance.
The unequal-variance Welch procedure uses its t statistic with separate variance estimates.
The source documents the selectivity ratio as a model-dependent diagnostic computed from a fitted PLS application.
The source documents the variable-importance-in-projection scores computed from a fitted PLS model.
The usual Woolf heterogeneity statistic for odds ratios uses an asymptotic chi-square reference under large-sample conditions.
